# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Puzzles

---

## I. By Primary Task Type

### A. Shading / Painting Cells
Puzzles where the core action is determining which cells to color black (or leave white).

#### A1. Shading with Number Constraints (numbers indicate adjacent/nearby black cells)
- **Akari** – Place light bulbs; numbers on black squares indicate adjacent bulb count; all white cells must be illuminated
- **Kurotto** – Numbers in circles indicate sum of contiguous black cell groups extending from the circle
- **Kurodoko** – Numbers indicate count of visible white cells in cardinal directions to nearest black cell or edge
- **Nurikabe** – Numbers define white island sizes; black cells form one connected wall with no 2×2 blocks
- **Norinori** – Exactly two black cells per bold-outlined region; black cells always in dominoes
- **Nuritwin** – Each region contains exactly two same-sized shaded blocks; all shading connected
- **Usowan** – Numbers show adjacent black cell count, but one number per region is wrong

#### A2. Shading to Form Rectangles / Geometric Shapes
- **Choco Banana** – Black groups must form rectangles/squares; white groups must *not* form rectangles/squares; numbers give area size
- **Shakashaka** – Place triangles so remaining white space forms rectangles/squares
- **Tilepaint** – Color entire tiles (all-or-nothing); diagonal-cell numbers constrain black cell counts in rows/columns

#### A3. Shading with Connectivity / Separation Constraints
- **Heyawake** – Room numbers give black cell count; no two black cells adjacent; white cells connected; white can't span 3+ rooms in a line
- **Nurimisaki** – Circle cells are white "promontories" (one white neighbor); no 2×2 same-color blocks; white connected
- **LITS** – Place one tetromino per region; no same-shape tetrominoes adjacent; all colored cells connected; no 2×2 colored blocks
- **Sto-stone** – Room numbers give black cell count; black cells within a room are contiguous; when "dropped" they fill the bottom half

#### A4. Shading by Elimination (given numbers, remove duplicates)
- **Hitori** – Black out duplicate numbers so no row/column repeats; no adjacent black cells; white cells connected

---

### B. Loop Drawing
Puzzles where the core action is drawing a single closed loop through cell centers.

#### B1. Loop with Circle Constraints
- **Masyu** – White circles: loop goes straight, must turn in adjacent cell. Black circles: loop turns, must go straight in both next cells
- **Mid-loop** – Black circles must be the midpoint of their straight loop segment
- **Dotchi-Loop** – Loop passes through all white circles (straight or turning uniformly per region); avoids black circles

#### B2. Loop with Region / Room Constraints
- **Moon-or-Sun** – Loop visits each room once; in each room passes through all moons or all suns; alternates between moon-rooms and sun-rooms
- **Suraromu** – Loop starts/ends at numbered circle; must cross all "gates" (dotted lines) exactly once; gate numbers specify crossing order
- **Nagareru** – Directional loop; arrows set loop direction; "wind" arrows constrain movement (cannot go against wind)

#### B3. Loop with Shading (hybrid loop + shading)
- **Yajilin** – Draw loop; place black cells (not on loop, not adjacent to each other); arrow-numbers indicate black cell count in that direction
- **Slitherlink** – Loop drawn on dot grid edges; numbers indicate how many of the 4 surrounding edges are used

---

### C. Path / Connection Drawing
Puzzles where the task is drawing paths or connections (not necessarily a single closed loop).

- **Numberlink** – Connect pairs of identical numbers with non-crossing, non-branching paths that fill the grid
- **Hashiwokakero** – Connect island-circles with 1 or 2 bridges; each island's number = total bridges; all islands connected; bridges don't cross
- **Pencils** – Identify pencil shapes (straight cell groups with tips); draw lines from tips through a number of cells equal to the pencil's number

---

### D. Region Division / Partitioning
Puzzles where the core action is dividing the grid into regions/blocks.

#### D1. Partitioning into Fixed-Size Regions
- **Five Cells** – Divide grid into pentominoes (5-cell blocks); numbers indicate bordering block-edge count
- **Shikaku** – Divide grid into rectangles; each rectangle contains exactly one number equal to its area

#### D2. Partitioning into Variable Regions with Constraints
- **Double Choco** – Divide grid so each block has matching white and gray sub-regions of identical shape
- **Sashigane** – Divide grid into L-shaped blocks; circles mark bends; arrows mark ends pointing toward bends; numbers give block size
- **Fillomino** – Fill grid with numbers; regions of same number have size equal to that number; same-size regions can't be adjacent

---

### E. Number / Symbol Placement
Puzzles where the core action is placing numbers or symbols into cells.

#### E1. Latin Square Variants
- **Sudoku** – Place 1–9 in each row, column, and 3×3 box

#### E2. Room-Based Number Placement
- **Ripple Effect** – Rooms get consecutive numbers from 1; if a number repeats in a row/column, the gap between them ≥ that number
- **Makaro** – Rooms get 1 through room-size; arrow cells point to the largest neighboring number; no same number adjacent across rooms

#### E3. Number Placement from a List
- **Nansuke** – Fill blank cells with digits from a given number list; numbers read left-to-right or top-to-bottom

#### E4. Fill with Symbols (not numbers)
- **Juosan** – Fill every cell with — or |; territory numbers constrain the majority symbol; no 3+ consecutive same symbols in the constrained direction

---

### F. Object Placement / Movement
Puzzles where the solver places or moves discrete objects.

#### F1. Placement of Objects
- **Akari** (also in A1) – Place light bulbs in white cells
- **Hebi** – Place numbered snakes (1–5 sequences) in white cells with visibility and adjacency constraints
- **Chained Block** – Determine which cells are black to form numbered blocks; blocks chain diagonally; chain has no duplicate block shapes
- **Evolomino** – Place growing polyomino blocks along arrows; each subsequent block adds one square to the previous shape

#### F2. Movement of Objects
- **Satogaeri** – Move circles within "countries" so each country has exactly one; number = cells traversed; paths can't cross
- **Yosenabe** – Move all circles straight into gray areas; arrows show paths; numbers in gray areas = sum of entering circle values

---

### G. Maze Construction
- **Nurimeizu** – Paint rooms black or white to create a maze from S to G; circles on shortest path, triangles not; no 2×2 same-color blocks

---

## II. By Constraint Mechanism (Cross-Cutting)

| Constraint Type | Puzzles |
|---|---|
| **Numbers = adjacent count** | Akari, Shakashaka, Slitherlink, Usowan, Five Cells |
| **Numbers = region/area size** | Shikaku, Fillomino, Choco Banana, Nurikabe, Nurimisaki, Sashigane, Double Choco, Nuritwin, Sto-stone |
| **Numbers = visible/reachable cells** | Kurodoko, Akari (illumination) |
| **Numbers = sum of groups** | Kurotto, Yosenabe |
| **Numbers = movement distance** | Satogaeri |
| **Numbers = sequence/order** | Hebi, Suraromu, Ripple Effect, Makaro |
| **No same-size/shape adjacency** | Fillomino, LITS, Chained Block |
| **Connectivity of white cells** | Hitori, Heyawake, Kurodoko, Nurikabe, Nurimisaki, Usowan |
| **Connectivity of black cells** | Nurikabe, LITS, Nuritwin, Sto-stone |
| **No 2×2 monochrome blocks** | Nurikabe, LITS, Nurimisaki, Nurimeizu |
| **No adjacent black cells** | Hitori, Heyawake, Yajilin, Usowan |
| **Room/region constraints** | Heyawake, Moon-or-Sun, Makaro, Ripple Effect, Double Choco, Five Cells, Norinori, Nuritwin, Sto-stone, Nurimeizu |
| **Directional arrows** | Yajilin, Makaro, Nagareru, Hebi, Sashigane, Evolomino, Yosenabe |

---

## III. By Grid Element Used

| Element | Puzzles |
|---|---|
| **Dots/vertices (lines on edges)** | Slitherlink, Hashiwokakero |
| **Cell centers (loop through cells)** | Masyu, Mid-loop, Yajilin, Dotchi-Loop, Moon-or-Sun, Suraromu, Nagareru |
| **Cell centers (paths, not loops)** | Numberlink, Pencils |
| **Cell shading (binary black/white)** | Nurikabe, Heyawake, Hitori, Kurodoko, Kurotto, Norinori, LITS, Nurimisaki, Choco Banana, Tilepaint, Usowan, Nuritwin, Sto-stone, Shakashaka, Akari, Nurimeizu, Chained Block |
| **Cell partitioning (drawing borders)** | Shikaku, Five Cells, Double Choco, Sashigane, Fillomino |
| **Number/symbol filling** | Sudoku, Fillomino, Ripple Effect, Makaro, Nansuke, Juosan |
| **Object placement/movement** | Akari, Hebi, Satogaeri, Yosenabe, Evolomino |
| **Mixed color grid (gray + white)** | Double Choco |

---

## IV. Visual Summary Tree

```
Grid-Based Logic Puzzles
│
├── SHADING PUZZLES
│   ├── Constraint: number = adjacent black cells
│   │   ├── Akari, Kurotto, Kurodoko, Usowan
│   │   └── Shakashaka (triangles, not full cells)
│   ├── Constraint: region/shape rules
│   │   ├── Choco Banana, Tilepaint
│   │   ├── LITS, Norinori, Nuritwin
│   │   └── Sto-stone
│   ├── Constraint: connectivity + separation
│   │   ├── Nurikabe, Heyawake, Nurimisaki
│   │   ├── Hitori, Nurimeizu
│   │   └── Chained Block
│   └── Constraint: duplicate elimination
│       └── Hitori
│
├── LOOP PUZZLES
│   ├── Circle-constrained loops
│   │   ├── Masyu, Mid-loop, Dotchi-Loop
│   │   └── Nagareru
│   ├── Region-constrained loops
│   │   ├── Moon-or-Sun, Suraromu
│   │   └── Dotchi-Loop
│   ├── Hybrid loop + shading
│   │   └── Yajilin
│   └── Edge-based loops
│       └── Slitherlink
│
├── PATH / CONNECTION PUZZLES
│   ├── Numberlink
│   ├── Hashiwokakero
│   └── Pencils
│
├── REGION DIVISION PUZZLES
│   ├── Fixed-size partitions
│   │   ├── Five Cells, Shikaku
│   │   └── Evolomino
│   ├── Variable partitions with shape matching
│   │   ├── Double Choco, Sashigane
│   │   └── Fillomino
│   └── Evolomino (progressive polyomino growth)
│
├── NUMBER / SYMBOL PLACEMENT
│   ├── Sudoku (Latin square)
│   ├── Ripple Effect, Makaro (room-based)
│   ├── Nansuke (list-based fill)
│   ├── Juosan (symbol fill: — and |)
│   └── Hebi (sequential number placement)
│
└── OBJECT MOVEMENT
    ├── Satogaeri (move circles into countries)
    └── Yosenabe (move circles into gray areas)
```
